message.content:
You are reverse-engineering a compiled C++ binary as a BLACK BOX. The C++ library source is NOT available and you must NOT look for it.

Binary: /workspace/dataset/test20_executable
Invoke: /workspace/dataset/test20_executable '<word>'      (exactly one argument)
It prints exactly 20 lines to stdout, one per API call, in this fixed order (1-indexed):
  1  pluralize(word)
  2  singularize(word)
  3  camelize(word)                       // default 2nd param
  4  camelize(word, false)
  5  underscore(word)
  6  classify(word)
  7  tableize(word)
  8  humanize(word)
  9  titleize(word)
  10 dasherize(word)
  11 parameterize(word)
  12 parameterize("A " + word + " Test")
  13 upcase(word)
  14 downcase(word)
  15 capitalize(word)
  16 decapitalize(word)
  17 truncate(word, 5)
  18 demodulize("Test::" + word)
  19 to_string(isPlural(word))    -> "0"/"1"
  20 to_string(isSingular(word))  -> "0"/"1"

With no argument it prints nothing. With an empty argument it ABORTS (std::out_of_range from
basic_string::substr inside demodulize) printing nothing to stdout.

TOOLING TIPS
- Extract one line:  /workspace/dataset/test20_executable 'word' | sed -n '5p'
- Show exact bytes:  /workspace/dataset/test20_executable 'word' | sed -n '5p' | od -c
- Loop:  for w in a b c; do printf '%s -> ' "$w"; /workspace/dataset/test20_executable "$w" | sed -n '5p'; done
- Use $'...' bash quoting for control bytes / high bytes, e.g. $'a\tb', $'\xc3\xa9'.
- 'file' is unavailable; 'strings', 'od', 'sed', 'nl' work.
- The binary is fast; run HUNDREDS of probes. Be exhaustive, not economical.

GROUND RULES
- Every claim in your output MUST be backed by an observed probe you actually ran.
- Assume C locale: toupper/tolower/isalnum/isspace behave as ASCII-only; bytes >= 0x80 are
  unchanged by case ops and are NOT alnum. VERIFY this rather than assuming.
- Note operations are byte-based (std::string), not char-based. Test multi-byte UTF-8.
- Report the algorithm as precise pseudocode that a Rust programmer can transcribe with zero guessing,
  operating on BYTES.


YOUR ASSIGNMENT (cli_edges):
Characterize the PROGRAM-level behavior, not individual APIs.
 - No arguments: exact stdout (should be empty), exit code.
 - Empty string argument: exact stdout, stderr, exit code (expected abort/134). Confirm nothing is
   printed to stdout before the abort.
 - More than one argument: is argv[2] ignored? (/workspace/dataset/test20_executable a b)
 - Arguments that look like flags: "-h", "--help", "-", "--".
 - Argument containing a newline, tab, NUL-adjacent bytes, very long (10k chars) string.
 - Invalid UTF-8 raw bytes (use $'\xff\xfe').
 - Exit code in the normal case.
 - Confirm output is exactly 20 lines each terminated by '\n' including the last one
   (check with od -c | tail).
 - Whether stdout is line-buffered / any trailing output.
Report precisely, including exact exit codes and whether stdout ends with a newline.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

apis.pseudocode:
main(argc, argv):
    # NO flag parsing whatsoever. No getopt. No "--" handling. No usage text.
    if argc < 2:                       # i.e. no argument supplied
        return 0                       # writes ZERO bytes to stdout AND stderr
                                       # (verified: 0 write() syscalls at all)
    word = bytes_of(argv[1])           # raw bytes, NOT validated as UTF-8
    # argv[2], argv[3], ... are read but NEVER used; output is byte-identical
    # to running with argv[1] alone.

    # STEP 1: compute ALL 20 result strings FIRST (nothing is printed yet).
    r[1]  = pluralize(word)
    r[2]  = singularize(word)
    r[3]  = camelize(word)
    r[4]  = camelize(word, false)
    r[5]  = underscore(word)
    r[6]  = classify(word)
    r[7]  = tableize(word)
    r[8]  = humanize(word)
    r[9]  = titleize(word)
    r[10] = dasherize(word)
    r[11] = parameterize(word)
    r[12] = parameterize("A " + word + " Test")
    r[13] = upcase(word)
    r[14] = downcase(word)
    r[15] = capitalize(word)
    r[16] = decapitalize(word)
    r[17] = truncate(word, 5)
    r[18] = demodulize("Test::" + word)     # <-- THE ONLY THROWING CALL
    r[19] = isPlural(word)   ? "1" : "0"
    r[20] = isSingular(word) ? "1" : "0"

    # STEP 2: print them.
    for i in 1..=20:
        write(stdout, r[i]); write(stdout, "\n"); flush(stdout)

    return 0

# Because step 1 fully precedes step 2, when demodulize throws NOTHING has been
# written to stdout — this is NOT a buffering artifact (proved with stdbuf -o0
# and with a gdb syscall trace showing 0 write(fd=1) calls).

apis.name: ABORT condition (empty arg, and any arg ending in ':')
apis.pseudocode:
# The ONLY way the program dies abnormally by its own doing is line 18,
# demodulize("Test::" + word), which does an unchecked substr.
#
# Let s = "Test::" + word   (len(s) == 6 + len(word))
# Let p = last index of byte ':' (0x3A) in s          # always exists: s[4], s[5]
# demodulize returns s[p+2 ..]   -- NOTE the +2, not +1 (an off-by-one in the lib)
# std::string::substr throws std::out_of_range iff  p + 2 > len(s).
#
# p == len(s) - 1  <=>  s ends with ':'  <=>  word is EMPTY (s ends with the
#                       second ':' of "Test::")  OR  word ends with ':'.
# In that case p + 2 == len(s) + 1 > len(s)  ->  THROW  ->  no catch  ->

# On abort:
#   stdout: 0 bytes. Nothing at all, not even a partial line. (All 20 values are
#           computed before any printing, so the throw happens before print #1.)
#   stderr: exactly 147 + (digits) bytes, two lines, in 6 separate write(2) calls:
#       "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::out_of_range'\n"
#       "  what():  basic_string::substr: __pos (which is P) > this->size() (which is S)\n"

#           bash additionally prints "Aborted (core dumped)" to ITS stderr

#
# Everything else (including words that merely CONTAIN ':' but do not end with
# one: "a:b", ":a", "::a", "a:b:c") runs normally and exits 0.

edge_cases: The abort is by SIGNAL, not by exit(): raw wait status is signal 6 with code 0. A Rust reimplementation must call std::process::abort() (or libc::raise(SIGABRT)) — `std::process::exit(134)` is observably different to a parent that inspects WIFSIGNALED.
No output is lost to buffering on abort: proven with stdbuf -o0, stdbuf -oL, a pty, and a gdb syscall trace. The program genuinely computes all 20 results before printing any.
Words that merely contain ':' are fine; only a TRAILING ':' (or an empty word) aborts.
The numbers in the what() message are derived from the word length: __pos = len(word)+7, size = len(word)+6. Format has two spaces before 'what():' and two spaces after it.
An empty argv[1] aborts even when argv[2] is present and non-empty.
bash's "Aborted (core dumped)" text is emitted by the shell, not the program; whether "(core dumped)" appears depends on `ulimit -c`.

apis.name: Output framing: exactly 20 newline-terminated records
apis.pseudocode:
# Framing contract:
#   * On success the program emits exactly 20 RECORDS.
#   * Each record = the API result bytes, immediately followed by ONE 0x0A.
#   * The 20th record IS newline-terminated: the last byte of stdout is 0x0A.
#   * There is no header, no BOM, no separator, no trailing blank line,
#     no output after record 20, and no \r anywhere (any \r\n seen is a pty's
#     ONLCR translation, not the program).
#   * Records may be EMPTY (just a bare \n) — e.g. parameterize of a
#     non-alnum word, or demodulize of a word containing ':'.
#
# CAVEAT for line counting: "20 lines" == "20 records". The record payload is
# raw bytes copied from argv, so if the word itself contains 0x0A the payload
# contains literal newlines and `wc -l` will report MORE than 20.
#   word = "a\nb"  -> 36 total 0x0A bytes on stdout (20 record terminators
#                     + 16 embedded, because 16 of the 20 results echo the
#                     word's newline).
#   word = "\n"    -> 35 total 0x0A bytes, 46 bytes of stdout.
# So a differential test harness must compare BYTES, or split on the known
# 20-record structure, not on newlines.
#
# Nothing is ever written to stderr on the success path (0 bytes).

apis.name: stdout buffering / flush behavior / write error handling
apis.pseudocode:
# BUFFERING: the program FLUSHES AFTER EVERY RECORD (std::endl semantics),
# regardless of whether stdout is a tty, a pipe, or a regular file.
# A gdb syscall-1 trace with stdout redirected to a REGULAR FILE (which glibc
# would normally fully-buffer in 4096-byte chunks) shows exactly 20 write(2)
# calls on fd 1, one per record, each of length == len(record)+1.
#
#   for 'word':  6,5,5,5,5,5,6,5,5,5,5,12,5,5,5,5,5,4,2,2
#                ^ "words\n"                  ^ "a-word-test\n"   ^ "0\n","1\n"
#
# So there is NO buffered tail to lose, and output ordering is observable
# incrementally by a reader on a pipe.
#
# WRITE ERRORS ARE SILENTLY IGNORED (no check of the stream state, no
# diagnostic, no non-zero exit):
#   stdout closed  (>&-)        -> exit 0, empty stderr
#   stdout /dev/full (ENOSPC)   -> exit 0, empty stderr
#
# SIGPIPE IS NOT IGNORED/HANDLED: default disposition. If the reader closes
# early and the program still has data to write, it dies with signal 13.
# (Rust's default is the OPPOSITE — Rust sets SIGPIPE to SIG_IGN, so a naive
#  Rust port would get EPIPE + exit 0 instead of dying with 141. Restore the
#  default handler if that difference matters to your harness.)
#
# Not observable-relevant but recorded: the binary does not reference
# std::ios_base::sync_with_stdio (no such symbol), and does reference
# std::ostream::flush (_ZNSo5flushEv), consistent with per-line std::endl.

evidence.output: 20 distinct write(fd=1) calls (each reported twice, on syscall entry and return) with len = 6,5,5,5,5,5,6,5,5,5,5,12,5,5,5,5,5,4,2,2 — i.e. one flushed write per record, no 4096-byte block buffering
EXIT=0, stderr empty — write failures are silently ignored
EXIT=0, stderr empty — no error checking, no diagnostic, no failure exit code

evidence.input: perl: fork+pipe, read only 100 bytes of the output for a 120000-byte word, then close the read end
evidence.output: sig=13 code=0 => killed by SIGPIPE (default disposition). Same case via shell subshell: PROG_EXIT=141
prints 'words', PIPESTATUS[0]=0 — output is small enough to fit in the 64 KiB pipe buffer, so no SIGPIPE; the signal only appears with large output

evidence.input: strings -a on the binary, grep for sync_with_stdio / flush
evidence.output: 0 hits for sync_with_stdio; `_ZNSo5flushEv` and `_ZNSo5flushEv@GLIBCXX_3.4` present — consistent with per-line std::endl and default stdio syncing

edge_cases: Per-record flush means a reader on a pipe sees each of the 20 records as a separate write(2); do not assume the output arrives as one blob.
Write errors (EBADF from a closed fd 1, ENOSPC from /dev/full) never change the exit code — it stays 0 and stderr stays empty.
SIGPIPE uses the default action -> exit status 141 when the consumer quits early on large output. Rust ignores SIGPIPE by default, so a port must explicitly restore SIG_DFL to match.
Small outputs (a few hundred bytes) never trigger SIGPIPE with `| head -1` because they fit entirely in the pipe buffer; you need >64 KiB of output to observe it.

uncertainties: The 131072-byte argument ceiling is the Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN (32 pages), not a property of the binary. On a kernel with a different page size the cutoff would move. Verified only on this host: 131071 works, 131072 fails with E2BIG / bash exit 126.

Embedded NUL bytes in argv[1] are impossible to test at all — execve argv entries are NUL-terminated C strings. I confirmed bash truncates at the first NUL (printf '%s' $'a\x00b' emits only 'a'), so the program can never observe one. Any Rust port using OsString from argv inherits the same property; no divergence is possible.
bash's "(core dumped)" annotation on the SIGABRT cases depends on `ulimit -c` in this container; the signal itself (SIGABRT/6 -> status 134) is the program-level fact and is stable.

The claim that all 20 results are computed before any printing is inferred from (a) zero write(fd=1) syscalls before the throw and (b) per-record flushing on the success path. That is airtight for observable behavior, but I cannot distinguish a std::vector<std::string> built up front from any other construct that has the same ordering.

I verified locale independence for the 0xE9 byte across C/POSIX/UTF-8/ISO-8859-1/ISO-8859-9 locales via LC_ALL, LANG, and LC_CTYPE. I did not exhaustively test every high byte under every locale, but the absence of any locale symbol usage and the uniform result make setlocale() being uncalled very likely.

The exact per-API semantics (pluralize, demodulize's +2 off-by-one, etc.) are outside my assignment; I only characterized demodulize far enough to establish the exact abort predicate (word empty or word ends with ':'), which I validated against 585 randomized words with zero mismatches.
